main_theorems.label: Theorem 1.1 (thm:main)
main_theorems.statement: There is no algorithm which, given a polynomial $f\in\Z[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$, with $n$ part of the input, decides whether $f$ has a zero in $\Q^n$.
main_theorems.hypotheses: Stated unconditionally. The proof (Prop. 2.14 red:finite-test-success + parallel search, 02-reduction.tex:755-887) rests on: DPRM theorem (published); Prop. 2.2 rank E(Q(sqrt2))=1 for y^2=x^3-d^2x, d=75-53sqrt2 (proved, 2-isogeny descent); Prop. 2.3 formal-log estimates (proved); Thm 2.4 five-point height estimate (proved MODULO OAI 'Fontaine-Mazur modularity at the prime 2' Thm 1.1); Prop. 2.9 pole-parity formula (proved MODULO OAI 'pointwise 2-converse' Thm 1.1); Lemma 6.1 prime patterns (Green-Tao-Ziegler, published). So the theorem is conditional on two unrefereed OAI companions.

main_theorems.label: Corollary 7.1 (thm:degree-normal-form)
main_theorems.statement: With the usual effective coding, let $\mathrm{H10}(\Q)$ be the set of integral polynomials having a rational zero, with the number of variables part of the input. Then $\mathrm{H10}(\Q)$ has Turing degree $0'$, the degree of the halting problem. The same is true for each of the following restricted input problems: (i) rational solvability for integral polynomials of total degree at most four; (ii) given a nonempty finite list $q_1,\ldots,q_s\in\Z[X_1,\ldots,X_N]$, each of total degree at most two, whether $\sum_{i=1}^s q_i^2$ has a zero in $\Q^N$. No bound is imposed on the number of variables, the number of summands in (ii), or the coefficient heights.
main_theorems.hypotheses: Same inputs as Theorem 1.1 (the finite-test Turing reduction H10(Z) <=_T H10(Q)) plus Davis 1973 Thm 8.1/7.5 and the four-square theorem. Manuscript states it 'does not establish many-one completeness of H10(Q)' and 'gives no single existential definition of Z in Q'.

general_results.label: Lemma 3.4 (par:descent): 2-Selmer rank of y^2=x(x-l)(x+3l) via Monsky/Redei matrices
general_results.statement: Let $l>0$ be squarefree, prime to $6$, with $l\equiv3\pmod4$ and $l\equiv2\pmod3$. Suppose that its support $Q$ contains the nonempty set $B$ of Lemma~3.3 and a prime outside $B$, and suppose that $\ker K=\langle\mathbf1,\mathbf1_B\rangle$, $\lambda\notin\operatorname{im}K$. Then $\dim_{\F_2}\Sel_2(E_l/\Q)=3$, and $(\beta,1)$ is a Selmer class outside the subgroup of rational two-torsion classes, in Kummer coordinates $(x+3l,x-l)$.
general_results.hypotheses: Specific one-parameter family E_l: y^2=x(x-l)(x+3l) with FULL rational 2-torsion; l squarefree, (l,6)=1, l=3 mod 4, l=2 mod 3; Legendre-symbol matrix conditions (par:matrices, par:matrix-target). Proved in the manuscript by full 2-descent with explicit local images at odd q, at 3, a necessary condition at 2, and the real place (Silverman X.1.4, X.4.2; Monsky appendix in Heath-Brown 1994; Wei-Guo 2022).
general_results.relevance: none: the seed E has E(Q)_tors = Z/2 (not full 2-torsion) and is not in this family; Sha(E)[2]=0 is already known.

general_results.label: Lemma 3.5 (par:global-point) proof step: Cassels-Tate parity of dim Sha[2]
general_results.statement: The Cassels--Tate pairing on this finite group is perfect and alternating ... Hence $\dim_{\F_2}\Sha(E_l/\Q)[2]$ is even. This conclusion uses the perfect pairing on the full finite $2$-primary group; its restriction to the subgroup killed by $2$ need not be perfect.
general_results.hypotheses: Sha(E/Q) finite (here obtained from the imported 2-converse); principal polarization from the divisor (O); Cassels 1962, Poonen-Stoll 1999 Cor. 9.
general_results.relevance: none (standard published fact; the seed's Sha[2]=0 and Sha[3^infty]=(Z/3)^2 are consistent with it and already recorded).

general_results.label: Proposition 2.2 (ell:rank)
general_results.statement: The group $E(F)$ has rank one. Consequently there exist a positive integer $m$ and a nontorsion point $P\in E(F)$ such that $mE(F)=\Z P$. We fix such $m$ and $P$ once and for all.
general_results.hypotheses: F=Q(sqrt2), d=75-53sqrt2 (norm 7), E: y^2=x^3-d^2x (specific CM-by-Q(i) twist). Proved by 2-isogeny descent over the PID Z[sqrt2] (sections/05-elliptic.tex:20-101). The rank-one point Q=(-dw, 2sqrt2 d^2), w=-5+4sqrt2.

general_results.label: Theorem 2.4 (hei:height): Five-point height estimate
general_results.statement: There exist five distinct points $\mathcal C\subset\mathbf P^1(\Q)$, including $\infty$, a finite set $S$ of rational primes, and constants $H,c>0$ with the following property. For each $b\in\mathcal C$, choose a primitive integral linear form $L_b(U,V)$ vanishing at $b$, with $L_\infty(U,V)=V$. For $s=(u:v)\in\mathbf P^1(\Q)\setminus\mathcal C$, let $M_S(s)$ be the product, taken without repetition, of primes $q\notin S$ for which at least one of the integers $v_q(L_b(u,v))-\min\{v_q(u),v_q(v)\}$, $b\in\mathcal C$, is odd. Then $\hgt(s)\le H M_S(s)^c$.
general_results.hypotheses: C = the five branch values of the Atkin-Lehner quotient X^* of the discriminant-210 Shimura curve (genus 5 -> P^1). Proof: QM abelian-surface family over a fine level Y, Pazuki theta/Faltings comparison, Q-curve-type descent cocycle, OAI Fontaine-Mazur modularity at 2 (black box, no residual-image hypothesis), Carayol local-global compatibility, Javanpeykar Belyi height bound for J_1(N), Gaudron-Remond isogeny theorem, Zarhin trick, Bost lower bound. Ineffective constants (CM case uses ineffective class-number finiteness).
general_results.relevance: none for BSD obligations. (Note the manuscript's own list of related published bounds: von Kaenel 2013 Prop 9.9, von Kaenel-Kret 2023 Thm 7.1, 04-height.tex:1311-1326.)

general_results.label: Proposition 2.9 (par:pole-parity)
general_results.statement: There are a positive existential formula $\Phi(b)$ in the language of rings, with fixed rational coefficients, and a finite set $S_1$ of rational primes such that: (1) $\Q\models\Phi(b)$ for every $b\in\Z$; (2) if $b\in\Q^\times$ and $\Q\models\Phi(b)$, then, for every $q\notin S_1$, the inequality $v_q(b)<0$ implies $v_q(b)\in2\Z$.
general_results.hypotheses: Soundness (2) is proved elementarily (Lemma 3.1). Integer completeness (1) requires realizing a 2-Selmer class of y^2=x(x-l)(x+3l) by a rational point for two parameters l=n, n*theta, which uses the imported OAI pointwise 2-converse (Lemma 3.5) and the simultaneous Monsky-matrix construction (Lemma 3.6, Dirichlet + CRT).

general_results.label: Lemma 6.1 (pri:pattern): Prime patterns
general_results.statement: There is a finite set $\mathcal K\subset\Z_{>0}$ such that, for every $A\in\Z$ and every real $B>0$, there exist integers $u_1,u_2,v$, with $v\ne0$, for which, on setting $u_3=Av-u_1-u_2$, each of the thirteen numbers $v$, $L_b(u_j,v)$ ($1\le j\le3$, $b\in\mathcal C\setminus\{\infty\}$) has the form $\epsilon kr$, where $\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}$, $k\in\mathcal K$, and $r>B$ is a positive rational prime. Every such prime splits in $F$ and is a prime of good reduction for both $E$ and $E^\sigma$. At either place of $F$ above $r$, if $d_1,d_2$ are the cardinalities of the reduction groups of $E,E^\sigma$ over $\F_r$, then $\gcd(d_1,d_2)\mid4$, $r\nmid d_1d_2$.
general_results.hypotheses: r = 1 mod 8, r = 3 mod 7 so E, E^sigma reduce to opposite twists of y^2=x^3-x with orders r+1 +/- 2a. Proof: Green-Tao 2010 linear equations in primes (finite complexity, 13 affine-linear forms on Z^3) + Green-Tao 2012 + GTZ 2012 inverse theorem with 2024 erratum; Selberg upper sieve (Lemma 6.3) to remove common odd factors of the two group orders; Mertens in progressions (Williams 1974).

general_results.label: Corollary 6.2 (pri:integer-tests): Simultaneous integer tests
general_results.statement: Fix an integer $K\ge1$ and a prime $r$ supplied by Lemma 6.1, large enough for Proposition 2.3 at precision $K$. At each of the two places $v$ above $r$ there are nonzero integers $h,j_0$, chosen independently of $a\in\Z$, such that, for every $a\in\Z$: (1) $hP$ and $haP$ reduce to $O$ at $v$, $\ell_K(z(hP))\ne0$, and $v(\ell_K(z(haP))/\ell_K(z(hP))-a)\ge K$; (2) $j_0P^\sigma$ and $(h-4)aP^\sigma$ reduce to $O$ at the same place $v$, and $v(z((h-4)aP^\sigma)/z(j_0P^\sigma))\ge K$.
general_results.hypotheses: As in Lemma 6.1; proof by CRT using gcd(d_1,d_2)|4 and r does not divide d_1 (j_0=d_2, h=0 mod d_1, h=4 mod d_2 r^K).

general_results.label: Lemma 6.3 (pri:upper-sieve): two-dimensional Selberg upper sieve
general_results.statement: The number of points in this square avoiding every $\Omega_p$ is at most $n^2/G(Z)+O(nZ^6+Z^8)$, $G(Z)=\sum_{e\le Z\ \text{squarefree},\ p\mid e\Rightarrow p\in\mathcal P_Z}\prod_{p\mid e}g(p)/(1-g(p))$. The error constant is absolute.
general_results.hypotheses: Forbidden sets Omega_p in F_p^2 of density g(p) in (0,1/2); square of side n in Z^2; Selberg lambda^2 method.

applicability.seed_E: NOT APPLICABLE. The manuscript proves no statement about a general elliptic curve over Q; its only general-EC statements are IMPORTED (2-converse theorems requiring corank_{Z_2} Sel_{2^infty} <= 1). For the seed E, rank 2 forces every p^infty-Selmer corank >= 2, so K-RANK2 kills both imported theorems. The 2-Selmer matrix lemma (Lemma 3.4) is for y^2=x(x-l)(x+3l) with full rational 2-torsion; E has E(Q)_tors = Z/2 and is not in that family. Nothing touches FIN, ORDER9, Q36, Sha[p^infty] at any prime, lemma TH, or the Brandt/B.18 cost. No Iwasawa main conjecture, Euler system, control theorem, p-adic L-function, Heegner/theta, parity, Tamagawa, twist-distribution, level-raising, additive-prime, or anticyclotomic statement appears anywhere in the manuscript.

The imported pointwise 2-converse (Thm 1.1 of the companion) has hypotheses that E^{-7} satisfies: E^{-7}(Q)[2] != 0 (the quadratic twist keeps the 2-torsion point (0,0)) and corank_{Z_2} Sel_{2^infty}(E^{-7}/Q) = 0. The companion is not proved in this manuscript, and nothing here gives #Sha(E^{-7}) or any BSD leading-term formula. Even if the companion were accepted at grade IMPORTED_PREPRINT it would be strictly weaker than the existing PROVED chain.
